question.name: triv1
question.text: Which area often suffered from droughts, blizzards, hail, and grasshoppers?

explanation.name: right1
explanation.text: Between 1880 and 1950, farmers in the Great Plains states faced all these natural disasters.

question.name: triv2
question.text: Who gave the Statue of Liberty to the Americans?

explanation.name: right2
explanation.text:
The French gave the Statue of Liberty to the Americans in 1886, to celebrate America's 100th birthday. It is a larger copy of a statue that stands on the bank 
of the Seine River in Paris.  
Frederic Auguste Bartholdi created the nine-foot original.  The New York  version is a copper and steel structure created 
by Gustave Eiffel (the builder of the Eiffel Tower). The 152-foot-tall Statue of Liberty stands on Liberty Island in New York harbor.  In her left hand, Liberty holds a book that symbolizes the Declaration of Independence.  In her right hand, she holds the torch of freedom.

question.name: triv3
question.text: What caused Teddy Roosevelt to return to politics in New York?

answers.name: ans31
answers.text: A. the start of the Civil War

answers.name: ans32
answers.text:
B. droughts and blizzards on 
      the Great Plains

answers.name: ans33
answers.text: C. opposition to the Jim Crow laws

answers.name: ans34
answers.text: D. the failure of his family business

explanation.name: right3
explanation.text: In 1884, Theodore Roosevelt left the New York Legislature and moved to North Dakota to be a farmer.  Unfortunately, the Great Plains were suffering from terrible droughts that killed most of the cattle there.  In 1886, Theodore Roosevelt gave up his farm and returned to his political career in New York.

question.name: triv4
question.text: In 1889, homesteaders rushed to stake out land that the government was giving away.  What was this called?

explanation.name: right4
explanation.text: In 1889, the U.S. government opened part of the Oklahoma territory to homestead settlement.  Thousands of homesteaders rushed to stake out land for themselves.  This was called "The Oklahoma Land Rush."  This land had originally been promised to Native American tribes who had hoped for their own state.

question.name: triv5
question.text: How many states are named after American presidents?

explanation.name: right5
explanation.text:
In 1889, the state of Washington joined the United States.  
Named in honor of  George Washington, it is the only state named after a president.

question.name: triv6
question.text:
What did  Whitcomb L. Judson invent 
in 1891 that made  wearing trousers easier?

explanation.name: right6
explanation.text: In 1891, Whitcomb L. Judson invented the zipper when he decided that laces, hooks and eyes, and buttons took too long to fasten and unfasten.  Unfortunately, the zipper that Judson invented often came apart without warning.  In 1912, a Swedish engineer named Widen Sundback improved and patented the zipper, making it a popular fastener for clothing.

question.name: triv7
question.text: Who invented the game of basketball?

explanation.name: right7
explanation.text: Dr. James Naismith, born in Canada, was a physical education professor at the YMCA college in Springfield, Massachusetts.  He invented the game of basketball in December 1891.  Professional basketball games began in New York City in 1896.

question.name: triv8
question.text: Who set up the first large steel company in America?

explanation.name: right8
explanation.text:
Andrew Carnegie (1835-1919) founded the Carnegie Steel Company in 1892.  Carnegie was born in Scotland and came to America in 1848.  He was very poor and earned only $1.20 per week at his first job in America. He became very successful. In 1901, his steel company was bought by J. P. Morgan for $480 million, making Carnegie the richest man in the world.  Morgan combined Carnegie's company with other steel properties 
to create the United States Steel Company, which controlled 65 percent of all U.S. steel manufacturing.

question.name: triv9
question.text:
Which American president was killed in 1901 at the Pan-American Exposition, 
in Buffalo, New York?

explanation.name: right9
explanation.text:
President William McKinley was 
shot and killed at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, 
in 1901.  He was the 24th president 
of the United States.  
He was a Republican.

question.name: triv10
question.text: Who piloted the first flight of this motorized airplane in 1903?

explanation.name: right10
explanation.text: Wilbur and Orville Wright were the pilots of this plane, the Wright Flyer.  They became interested in flying by watching how flying birds twist their wing tips to balance.  For many years, they built flying machines that could fly without engines.  On December 17, 1903, in North Carolina, they made the first piloted flight in an airplane with a motor.  This flight changed the world.  The flight lasted 12 seconds, and the airplane flew nearly 200 feet.  Only nine days earlier, the New York Times had said that man would not fly for 1,000 years.

question.name: triv11
question.text: What kind of car is this?

explanation.name: right11
explanation.text:
This Model T was introduced by Henry Ford (1863-1947) in 1908.  
It was the first automobile that was successfully mass-produced for the ordinary citizen.  In 1913, Ford built 1,000 Model T cars each day.

question.name: triv12
question.text: Which products did the 1908 song, "Take Me Out to the Ball Game," promote?

answers.name: ans121
answers.text: A. Welch's Grape Juice and Pepsi-Cola

answers.name: ans123
answers.text: C. Planter's Peanuts and Cracker Jacks

answers.name: ans124
answers.text:
D. Hershey's Chocolate and Tootsie
      Rolls

explanation.name: right12
explanation.text: All these products were available in 1908, but only peanuts and Cracker Jacks were mentioned in the song.

question.name: triv13
question.text: Which problem did the Homestead Enlargement Act of 1909 try to solve?

answers.name: ans131
answers.text:
A. Native Americans were being forced
     onto reservations.

answers.name: ans132
answers.text: B. African Americans had few rights.

answers.name: ans133
answers.text:
C. A 160-acre farm  was not large
      enough to grow a decent crop.

answers.name: ans134
answers.text: D. Women were not allowed to vote.

explanation.name: right13
explanation.text:
There was very little rainfall in the Great Plains states.  A farm of 160 acres could not raise enough crops to support a homestead family.  In addition, ranchers needed bigger grazing areas.  The Homestead Enlargement Act of 1909 doubled the amount of land that Congress had given the farmers in the Homestead Act of 1862.  This was still not enough land for many farmers.  They continued to 
struggle for survival.

question.name: triv14
question.text:
This ship sank in April 1912.  
What is its name?

answers.name: ans143
answers.text: C. The Spirit of St. Louis

explanation.name: right14
explanation.text: This was the Titanic, a British luxury cruise ship.  In 1912, on its first trip from England to New York, it sank.  Of the 2,224 people on board, 1,513 drowned.  This was the worst sea disaster ever.

question.name: triv15
question.text:
This canal opened in 1914. 
What is it called?

explanation.name: right15
explanation.text:
The Panama Canal was completed in 1914.  It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.  Ships can use the canal to go from one ocean to the other, without traveling around the 
tip of South America.  The canal 
was built by the United States, 
which still owns it.  According to an agreement that was signed in 1978, the country of Panama will take 
over full control of the canal in 1999.

question.name: triv16
question.text: Which ray was discovered by Wilhelm Roentgen in 1895?

explanation.name: right16
explanation.text: Wilhelm C. Roentgen, a German scientist, discovered the X ray in 1895. It is a powerful ray of light that can pass through things that ordinary rays of light cannot enter.  X rays are used to take pictures of parts of the body that cannot be seen from the outside, such as organs and bones.  Roentgen called these rays X rays because he did not completely understand them.
